title: It's not height adjustable, so I don't get the point of this...
text:
It's not height adjustable, so I don't get the point of this.... JAN. 15, 2022 UPDATE:
---------------------------
* Since my review, they've removed the stock photo I mentioned that I thought was misleading, that made me think the box was height adjustable. This is a nice box. Probably more suited for your children's room than for the garage. I just think paying a higher price for the collapsing feature doesn't make sense. I thought the price was tied to the "adjustable" feature. There is no such feature, and the stock photo has been removed.

ORGINAL REVIEW:
----------------------

THE GOOD:
--------------
* Spacious 42L at about 17.5 x 13 x 13.
* Stackable.. that's it, that's all that's good.

THE BAD:
-----------
* Their 6th stock photo mislead me. I thought this box was height adjustable. I got it because I thought if I had any issues with clearance, I can just lower the height of the box. That's not the case at all. That stock photo is just showing you how thin it is when it's shipped to you.
* Lots of parts... you got the main frame, you got the bottom plate, you got a bumper guard that goes over the frame to give it stability, then lastly, you got the lid. When I was putting it together, I was asking myself, "What's the point of all this if it's not adjustable? Why not just get a sturdy one piece box?"
* All these moving parts, all this foldability design does not benefit you at all. It only benefits the manufacture because it allows them to save space when they ship them out. Think about that... the only time you'll fold this up, is if you don't use it. But why are you buying a box if you're not going to use it? I thought this thing was adjustable. I was thinking, wow, what a cool invention! LOL! It turns out, it's not. The fact that it folds benefits nobody but the company that sells it. Or, those rare occasions where you need to take a bunch of these boxes to some location. Realistically, how many are you going to buy at $42 a pop? If you're buying 5 to 10, and you need to transport them somewhere, yeah I get the benefit, you need to pack flat. Oh wait, I just described the company's scenario, right? LOL! They are selling hundreds or thousands of units, they need to pack flat to save on shipping!
* Price, these are not cheap. They are charging us more for a nifty design that benefits them, not us. Think about that. LOL!

In my garage, there is no point to all these moving parts, which are all points of potential failure. There are more economical solutions that are one piece (two with lid), and more sturdy than this box. BTW, I've seen the baskets that collapses at Costco, but I don't think twice about them because they don't cost $42 a pop. I don't understand the point of this design, if you have to charge consumers more for it because really, it doesn't benefit them. So I think 3 stars is generous.
